RULE-1.gloss: If x owns n units of legos priced at m dollars each and n×m=p, then x has earned p dollars
RULE-1.formula: ∀x∀n∀m∀p (Count(x, legos, n) ∧ PriceOf(x, legos, m) ∧ Product(n, m, p) → Money(x, earned, p))

RULE-2.gloss: If x buys n video games priced at m dollars each and n×m=p, then x has spent p dollars on cost
RULE-2.formula: ∀x∀n∀m∀p (Count(x, games, n) ∧ PriceOf(x, games, m) ∧ Product(n, m, p) → Money(x, cost, p))

RULE-3.gloss: If x earned n dollars and spent k dollars on cost, and n−k=r, then x has r dollars leftover
RULE-3.formula: ∀x∀n∀k∀r (Money(x, earned, n) ∧ Money(x, cost, k) ∧ Difference(n, k, r) → Money(x, leftover, r))

RULE-4.gloss: The number of additional Legos x could have sold equals the number of video games x bought
RULE-4.verify_reason: There is no basis for equating the number of Lego sets sold with the number of video games bought; the actual number sold must be derived from the money spent and left over (total spent + leftover = revenue from sales), not from the count of video games purchased.

RULE-5.gloss: If x owns n Lego sets and could have sold m additional Lego sets, and n−m=r, then x is left owning r Lego sets
RULE-5.formula: ∀x∀n∀m∀r (Count(x, legos, n) ∧ Count(x, additional_legos, m) ∧ Difference(n, m, r) → Count(x, legos, r))

INF-1.gloss: John earned $195 from selling Legos, from FACT-1, FACT-2, OP-1, and RULE-1 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-2.gloss: John spent $160 on video games, from FACT-3, FACT-4, OP-2, and RULE-2 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-3.gloss: John has $35 left over, from INF-1, INF-2, OP-3, and RULE-3 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-4.gloss: John could have sold 8 additional Lego sets, from FACT-3 and RULE-4 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-5.gloss: John is left owning 5 Lego sets, from FACT-1, INF-4, OP-4, and RULE-5 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

errors.message: There is no basis for equating the number of Lego sets sold with the number of video games bought; the actual number sold must be derived from the money spent and left over (total spent + leftover = revenue from sales), not from the count of video games purchased.
